newsitem.title: CHILE: U.S. Congress likely to grant fast-track - Gramm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Congress likely to grant fast-track - Gramm.

text.p: U.S. Senator Phil Gramm said Wednesday he thought Congress would grant President Bill Clinton special authority to negotiate international trade agreements and added a treaty between Chile and Canada should spur congressmen into supporting fast-track.

Gramm told reporters in Chile -- which wants to negotiate entry to the North American Free Trade Agreement -- that he thought Canada's deal with Chile would show congressional waverers that the United States had to act soon.
"This is a bus which has already left. The fact the bus has already left makes it more urgent that we get on it," Gramm said.
Asked whether he believed Congress would grant fast-track, he replied "Yes, I think so."

Chile's Chamber of Deputies last week approved a treaty with Canada to phase out trade barriers between the two countries by a vote of 78 to 21, with 10 abstentions. The deal, signed by President Eduardo Frei and Prime Minister Jean Chretien last year, still has to pass Chile's Senate.
